A 39-year-old male is brought to the emergency department by his roommates due to aggressive and
unusual behavior. His roommates report that he has been stressed from final exams, increasingly

withdrawn, and earlier in the evening was irritable, yelling at his computer before breaking it, and then
spending hours at the gym. His vital signs include a temperature of 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure of
133/88 mmHg, pulse of 113/min, respirations of 25/min, and oxygen saturation of 99% on room air.
Physical examination reveals an irritable and diaphoretic young man with dilated pupils, tachycardia,
and rapid speech. He is aggressive during the exam. After being treated with haloperidol,
diphenhydramine, and diazepam, and placed in soft restraints, his symptoms resolve over the next 10
hours. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Methamphetamine intoxication (B)
Serotonin syndrome (C) Alcohol withdrawal delirium (D) Phencyclidine intoxication (E) Acute mania
with psychosis (F) Cocaine intoxication (G) Lisdexamfetamine intoxication (H) Anticholinergic toxicity (I)
Hyperthyroidism-induced psychosis (J) Bath salts (synthetic cathinone) intoxication
 A. Hyperthyroidism-induced psychosis
B. Cocaine intoxication
